title: Pocket reads: quickfire notes on long-context caching & compression
content:
Purpose
- Quick, messy personal digest of papers / threads to keep in head while I try small experiments. Not a polished writeup.
- Goal: identify 2 low-effort ideas to prototype in serving runtime by end of sprint (3 weeks).

Key themes I'm tracking (one-liners)
- Compacting KV store entries: keep semantics but shrink per-key footprint (hashing + tiny embeddings vs full hidden states).
- Hybrid prefix caches: cache latent prefixes for popular prefixes + exact token-level KV for tail.
- Checkpointed attention maps: reconstruct context cheaply for low-memory long reads.
- Quantization interactions: 4-bit quant reduces footprint but hurts retrieval accuracy; need small distance-preserving transforms.

Papers / posts I skimmed (short notes)
- "Stochastic Compaction for KV Caches" (arXiv, 2025)
  - Idea: probabilistically merge adjacent KV slices for older context; reduces index size by ~3x at cost of mild drift for very long-range tokens.
  - Thoughts: could be applied as async GC job in runtime, prioritize by token recency + hit-rate.

- "Latent Prompt Reuse" (conference poster, 2025)
  - Store a compressed latent (small MLP projection of KV) per frequent prompt. Fast lookup + cheap rehydration.
  - Implementation note: need deterministic hashing of prompt normalization (lowercase+strip). Risk: prompt paraphrase variation reduces hits.

- "Sparse-Shard KV for Multi-Session" (github repo + blog)
  - Shard KV by session clusters to improve locality; less cross-session thrash.
  - Ops implication: routing layer needs to track cluster assignment; warmup can migrate hottest shards.

Interesting blog threads / slack notes
- @devin: observed >10% latency regressions when using 4-bit qKV on short (<=128) tails — might be kernel scheduling in cuda graph.
- internal note: we already store metadata per kv-entry (session id + position). Consider adding a 1-byte tag for "compressed-format" to avoid full deserialization.

Quick experiment ideas (prioritized)
1) Tiny-projection KV: store 64-d float16 projected vector alongside minimal key. Index with approximate NN (HNSW-lite).
   - Minimal infra: extend existing cache row schema, small service to rebuild ANN index every N minutes.
   - Success metric: same rerank hit rate within 3% while reducing stored bytes per entry by 4x.
   - Risks: ANN build time, serialization format drift between versions.

2) Probabilistic merge GC job (server-side background job)
   - Implementation: iterate old entries, if two consecutive entries from same session and low hit-rate, merge via average + timestamp range.
   - Success metric: 2x reduction in index size, <5% drop in perplexity on synthetic long-context eval.

3) Fast prefix cache (hybrid) prototype (low-effort)
   - Keep a small set (top 1k) of compressed latent prefixes (from training-time runs) + per-token KV for tail. Routing chooses latent prefix when exact-match score above threshold.
   - Implementation note: need evaluation harness to synthesize prefix hits; can reuse eval harness from /repos/long-context-evals.

Toy eval plan (very quick)
- Dataset: synthetic conversations (10k) + 100 real transcripts (internal). Use same prompt templates as redwood-evals/long-read.
- Metrics: PPL change, top-1 next-token match, API latency percentiles (p50/p95).
- Baseline: current uncompressed KV cache.
- Budget: run 1k sessions on a single A10 instance for quick signal.

Notes from local prototyping (commands & findings)
- Built small serializer: `python tools/kv_pack.py --mode=proj --dim=64` -> serializes to ~56 bytes/entry vs 232 bytes baseline (w/ full hidden states).
  - Readme: projection trained with MSE to original KV vector on heldout tokens; small degradation in cosine similarity (~0.06).
- Quick microbenchmark (A10): ANN lookup (HNSW) on 100k projected entries = ~1.8ms median, 5ms 95th. Good for p50 but need p95 improvement.
- Observed that saved memory allowed higher batch sizes which reduced per-token amortized cost. Win for throughput.

Open questions / unknowns
- How will rolling upgrades handle older cached formats? Need compatibility layer (tag byte + version).
- What threshold to use for merge GC? static TTL vs adaptive by hit-rate?
- Can we combine quantized storage with tiny projection without destroying ANN geometry? Potentially learn a quant-aware projection.

Next steps (this week)
- Sync quick 15m with Devin + Mika: share microbench numbers and get thumbs up for prototype 1. (TODO: Slack ping @devin)
- Flesh minimal on-disk schema + backward compat plan in 1 pager (target: 1 page) -> link into PR.
- Start small PR: extend cache row proto + add serializer. Keep default off behind a flag.

Loose links / references I want to re-read
- https://arxiv.org/abs/xxxxx (stochastic compaction paper)
- https://github.com/author/latent-prompt-reuse (poster code)
- internal deck: confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/long-context-plan (will link after tidy)

Random brain-dump (notes to self)
- If using ANN, consider adding tiny second-stage exact-check on rehydrated projection to avoid false positive prefix substitution.
- Add telemetry for matched-prefix ratio and average rehydration time.
- Small UX: expose cache format version in `x-cache-metadata` header for debugging.

End of pocket notes. Short, messy, actionable.
